about.heroSubtitle: History, Culture, Nature and Modern Life
about.introHeading: Heart of an Ancient Kingdom — Ujarma
about.introPara1: Ujarma is one of Georgia's most celebrated historic villages, located in Sagarejo Municipality in the Kakheti region. It is renowned for the Ujarma Fortress — one of the most significant royal residences of the early Middle Ages in the South Caucasus.
about.introPara2: Since the early Christian era of Georgia, Ujarma has held a special place in the history of Georgian statehood. In the 5th century, during the reign of King Vakhtang Gorgasali, Ujarma became one of the king's favored residences.
about.introPara3: Over the centuries, Ujarma has retained its agricultural character and its close bond with the land and viticulture. Today it is a place where history lives on in every stone and in the landscape itself.
about.historyPara1: The earliest mentions of Ujarma in old Georgian sources date to the 3rd–4th centuries. The ancient name "Ujarma" appears in the works of Vakhushti Bagrationi and in the chronicle "The Georgian Chronicles" (Kartlis Tskhovreba) as one of the most fortified strongholds of Kakheti.
about.historyQuote: In the 5th century, during the reign of Vakhtang Gorgasali, Ujarma became a favored seat of the royal court. The warrior-king often resided in this fortress during his campaigns in Kakheti.
about.historyPara2: In the 6th–7th centuries, as the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti developed, Ujarma solidified its role as a strategic military stronghold at the southern gateway to Kakheti. The route passing beneath the fortress served as a key thoroughfare for trade and military movement.
about.historyPara3: During the Middle Ages, amid various invasions of the country, Ujarma partly lost its former splendor, though the village itself survived. Today the fortress ruins stand under state protection as a monument of national cultural heritage.
about.timelineItem1Desc: First mention in the Chronicles of Georgia
about.geoPara1: Ujarma is situated on the north-western edge of the Kakheti plain-highland belt, in Sagarejo Municipality. The Iori River — one of the main rivers of Kartli-Kakheti — flows near the village.
about.geoPara2: The site lies at 400–600 metres above sea level. It is 60–65 km from Tbilisi, and Sagarejo is just 25 km away.
about.geoCard1Text: One of Kakheti's most beautiful natural landscapes, offering breathtaking panoramic views
about.geoCard2Text: Above sea level — ideal natural conditions for viticulture
about.geoCard3Text: Semi-arid: hot summers, mild winters, golden autumns
about.geoCard4Text: One hour by car — perfect for a day trip
about.culturePara: Kakheti is not only the cradle of Georgian wine, but also one of the richest centres of traditional Georgian culture.
about.cultureCard1Text: The people of Ujarma and neighboring villages preserve a centuries-old way of life: qvevri winemaking — a tradition inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
about.cultureCard2Text: The village calendar follows the cycle of the vine. At the end of summer, the grape harvest — the most joyful and family-centered celebration — is still held with as much spirit as it was ten generations ago.
about.cultureCard3Text: Ujarma's school, culture house, and local church are the axis of the village's social life. Annual gatherings, prayers, and historical celebrations form the village's most cherished wealth.
about.tourismPara: Having become one of the most important stops on Kakheti's tourist routes, Ujarma welcomes thousands of visitors every year.
about.tourismItem1Desc: A rocky hilltop facing the national monument dating from the 3rd–7th century
about.tourismItem2Desc: The stunning natural beauty of the Iori Valley
about.tourismItem3Desc: Local family wineries and traditional Kakhetian qvevri wine
about.tourismItem4Desc: Traditional Kakhetian feasts prepared by local families
about.tourismItem5Desc: The Vakhtang Gorgasali Trail — a 2–3 hour hike
about.tourismItem6Desc: An ideal spot — especially at dawn
about.tourismSubtext: Improving tourist infrastructure is one of the village administration's top priorities. Plans are under development for hospitality facilities and historic trail improvements.
about.adminPara: The Ujarma village administration is responsible for managing local infrastructure, delivering public services, and protecting the natural and cultural heritage of the village.
about.adminPara2: The administration operates in accordance with Georgian law, guided by the principles of full transparency and accountability.
about.adminQuote: "Our goal is a village where historical heritage is honored, young people return, and every resident proudly says: this is my village."
about.faq1A: Ujarma is located in Georgia's Kakheti region, in the Sagarejo municipality, about 60–65 kilometers from Tbilisi. The drive from the capital takes up to about an hour.
about.faq2Q: When was the Ujarma fortress built?
about.faq2A: The earliest structures of the Ujarma fortress date to the 3rd–4th centuries. The fortress reached particular grandeur in the 5th century, during the reign of Vakhtang Gorgasali, when it became one of the official residences of the royal court.
about.faq3A: Yes, the fortress grounds are open to visitors. As this is a cultural heritage site, please respect the environment and, where possible, join an organized tour with a local guide. For more information, contact the village administration.
about.faq4Q: Where can I taste Kakhetian wine?
about.faq4A: In the area around Ujarma there are several family wine cellars where local families offer visitors tastings of traditional Kakhetian wine, including qvevri wine. You can get an up-to-date list of local winemakers from the village administration.
about.faq5Q: Is there a hotel or guesthouse in the village?
about.faq5A: The village and surrounding area are working to improve tourism infrastructure. Currently, the most accessible option is guesthouse-style accommodation with local families or in nearby Sagarejo. The village administration will post updated information on this page.
about.faq6Q: What is the best time to visit?
about.faq6A: Kakheti is wonderful in three seasons. Spring (March–May) — nature blooms and the climate is mild. Summer (June–August) — sunny and warm, with vineyards full of fruit. Autumn (September–October) — Kakheti’s golden season, the grape harvest, and national traditions.
